author: Damien Bouissou
description: MCP server for the public stash-box metadata catalogues. Search scenes, performers, studios and tags across the public stash-box catalogues.
name: mcp-stashbox

tools.name: get_sources
tools.title: What each catalogue answers
tools.description: What each configured stash-box catalogue was measured answering, and the day its surface was read from it. Whether a key is held for a catalogue is a fact about this install and changes nothing about what the catalogue does. Reaches no catalogue and takes no argument.

identifier_prefix.description: The prefix a caller writes in front of a uuid.

key_configured.description: A fact about this install, and no fact about the catalogue.

answers.description: What it was measured answering, on the day named.

lacks.description: What it publishes no such thing for.

evidence.description: What the two lists rest on: a route seen answering, or one a schema declares.

measured_at.description: The day its surface was read from it.

tools.name: search_scenes
tools.title: Search scenes
tools.description: Search scenes across every configured stash-box catalogue. Two exclusive paths: 'query' runs each catalogue's own text index, which reads the words as a union, and the typed arguments narrow as an intersection. Writing both is refused. The answer says per catalogue which of three it met: a failure, a catalogue nobody asked, and an emptiness it established. Counts are never added across them.

query.description: Words for the catalogue's own text index, which reads them as a union. It is exclusive with the typed arguments, which narrow as an intersection.

alias.description: No catalogue's faceted route applies it, though every faceted input declares it: a request carrying it answers as wide as one carrying none, so it is never sent and the answer names it as a narrowing nobody received.

date_compare.description: These catalogues compare a date against one bound and answer no range, so the comparison is written rather than assumed.

match.description: How performer_ids and tag_ids are read, which are the only arguments it governs. 'all', the default, asks for scenes carrying every identifier of a list; 'any' for scenes carrying at least one, which answers counts an order of magnitude wider. A scene names one studio, so studio_ids asks for any of its identifiers under both readings. The lists narrow against each other as an intersection either way.

page.description: Which page of its own order every catalogue asked is read at, counted from 1. A search written with words alone reads the first rows each text index answers with, since those routes take no page.

limit.description: How many rows one page of one catalogue carries. An answer holding several carries up to this many from each: their pages are their own and nothing here interleaves them into one.

id.description: Written instance:uuid. The catalogue travels with the uuid.

source_url.description: The address it was read from. Credit the catalogue and link it.

retrieved_at.description: The moment this client read it there.

status.description: What the identifier addresses on that catalogue now. A folded record answers with a marker, which describes the record and never what it once named.

also_held_at.description: The same record on another catalogue, read from a link this one publishes to it. A shared name is no join.

linked_unfollowed.description: A link to another catalogue naming the record by something this client cannot address. The link is written, and following it is what failed.

pending_edits.description: Edits open against it, null where its catalogue publishes no such count.

pending_edits_unreadable.description: The count of open edits came back in a shape this client could not read.

rows_skipped.description: Entries of this record's own lists that could not be read and are left out.

rows_skipped_in.description: Which of its lists lost them.

code.description: The studio's own reference for the release.

duration_seconds.description: The runtime that catalogue holds, which is what separates two cuts of one title.

precision.description: How much of the date the catalogue holds: a month or a year can be all of it.

release_date_unreadable.description: A release date was published in a shape this client could not read, so the null above is a reading that failed rather than a date nobody entered.

production_date_unreadable.description: The same, for the production date, which get_scene answers with.

creditedAs.description: The name this release printed, where it differs.

tags.description: Each tag with the identifier the next call takes. What its catalogue filed it under is a fact about the tag, which get_tag answers.

result_count.description: How many rows this page carries.

source.description: The catalogue this row is about.

name.description: The name that catalogue calls itself.

state.description: 'answered' looked, and a count of zero means it found nothing. 'failed' could not answer, and states nothing about what it holds. 'absent' was never asked. Only the first is evidence about the world.

count.description: Rows it contributed. Never added to another catalogue's: they index corpora that overlap by an amount none of them publishes.

index_total.description: What its own index holds for the question it received, the rows on this page included. A narrowing it could not receive, or received in part, leaves that question wider than the one written.

index_total_over_any_word.description: The total counts rows carrying any word of the query, its text index reading them apart.

skipped.description: Rows it answered with that this client could not read and left out.

unattributed.description: Records it answered with while carrying none of what was asked about.

narrowings_not_received.description: Narrowings that shaped no part of the request this catalogue received, whether its route declares no field for one or nothing written was left for one to decide.

narrowings_naming_no_record.description: Narrowings written only with identifiers another catalogue minted.

narrowings_received_in_part.description: Narrowings it received short of what was written, the rest of the list naming records another catalogue minted. It answered a wider question than the one asked.

algorithms_not_searched.description: Fingerprint algorithms its lookup does not search, so they were never put to it.

reason.description: Why it was not asked, or what went wrong.

ordering.description: How the rows were laid out, which a reader needs before reading the first.

window.description: The page and the row limit this answer was read at, absent where no catalogue answered.

tools.name: get_scene
tools.title: Get one scene
tools.description: Read one scene from the catalogue its identifier names, written instance:uuid. The answer is one card, read on every catalogue that holds the record and reached by the link each of them publishes to the same record elsewhere. Every value names the catalogues that said it, and where they disagree the reading nobody preferred is published beside the one that won. Name 'sources' to read one catalogue alone.

sections.description: The blocks read beside the record's own fields, which come back whatever is written here. Each name adds a block, and 'basic' asks for those fields alone.

prefer.description: The order the catalogues are preferred in where they disagree on a field. Left out, the registry's own order stands, and every card states the order applied.

value.description: The reading the preference named, null where none published one.

agreed_by.description: The catalogues that published this reading. Two agreeing is evidence of its own.

disagreed.description: The readings nobody preferred, published rather than dropped: choosing between them is a policy, and a policy applied in silence is a claim nobody can check.

published_by.description: Every catalogue that published this very record. A shared name is no join, so an entry one catalogue minted names that one.

also_at.description: What this same record is called on another catalogue, from a link joining the two.

same_name_as.description: A record another catalogue published under a matching name. A resemblance, never a join.

fields.description: Each field of the record. A scalar carries the catalogues that said it; a list is the union, each entry naming who published it.

counts.description: Counts, one entry per catalogue asked and never added together. A null is read with the state beside it: a catalogue that publishes no such count, one that could not answer, and one nobody asked are three different facts.

source_url.description: The address it was read at, which credits it.

retrieved_at.description: The moment this client read it there.

status.description: What the identifier addresses there now. A folded record is held elsewhere.

held_by.description: Every catalogue asked, with the identifier the record carries there. This is where what each of them did with the record is read: the state says which of the three it met, and the reason says why it was not asked or what went wrong.

preferred.description: The order the readings were preferred in. This is the policy that was applied, whether or not every catalogue in it answered.

read_from.description: The catalogues that answered, in the order they were preferred. A policy and an outcome are two facts, and a reader deciding whether to change the policy needs both.

notes.description: What this answer does not establish, which is what makes it safe to act on.

MD5 and OSHASH name the bytes of a file; PHASH states a likeness a re-encode, a crop or another scene from one shoot can satisfy. match_kind.description: 'exact_file' names the same bytes. 'perceptual_similarity' covers a re-encode, a crop and another scene from one shoot, and is no evidence that two files are the same.

match_count.description: One per card here. Every hash that reached a record names it on one card, and a record reached both by an exact hash and by a perceptual one stands as two, since the two claim different things about it. Read records_named for how many files were named, which counts each once.

records_named.description: Distinct records an exact hash named. Two hashes reaching one record count once, and a perceptual match names no record.

resemblances.description: Matches a perceptual hash reached, each a likeness and no claim about any file's bytes.

unattributed.description: Records the catalogues answered with that carry none of the hashes asked. Which hash reached them is unknown, so they stand as no match and are counted apart.

unmatched.description: The hashes put to a catalogue that answered, which reached no record there. A catalogue named as unasked says nothing about them either way.

not_searched.description: Hashes and the catalogues that answered without searching their algorithm, so they were never put to those. Nobody looked there, which is no evidence about the files behind them.

source.description: The catalogue this row is about.

name.description: The name that catalogue calls itself.

state.description: 'answered' looked, and a count of zero means it found nothing. 'failed' could not answer, and states nothing about what it holds. 'absent' was never asked. Only the first is evidence about the world.

count.description: Rows it contributed. Never added to another catalogue's: they index corpora that overlap by an amount none of them publishes.

index_total.description: What its own index holds for the question it received, the rows on this page included. A narrowing it could not receive, or received in part, leaves that question wider than the one written.

index_total_over_any_word.description: The total counts rows carrying any word of the query, its text index reading them apart.

skipped.description: Rows it answered with that this client could not read and left out.

unattributed.description: Records it answered with while carrying none of what was asked about.

narrowings_not_received.description: Narrowings that shaped no part of the request this catalogue received, whether its route declares no field for one or nothing written was left for one to decide.

narrowings_naming_no_record.description: Narrowings written only with identifiers another catalogue minted.

narrowings_received_in_part.description: Narrowings it received short of what was written, the rest of the list naming records another catalogue minted. It answered a wider question than the one asked.

algorithms_not_searched.description: Fingerprint algorithms its lookup does not search, so they were never put to it.

reason.description: Why it was not asked, or what went wrong.
